## Independent deep review: #30679

Audited `b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f`. Three concrete counterexamples refine the original buffering plan; no audio/device run was performed.

### P1 — A corrected final frame can be silently discarded while marked final (reproduced)

Executed `/tmp/guardian-project19-deep-review/probe-30679.ts` with Bun. It extracts the unchanged production `queueAssistantSpeech` callback and real text-boundary/remainder helpers; collaborators capture tasks instead of playing audio. For the same message ID:

1. Streaming frame `The available option is red.` queues that sentence.
2. Final frame `Actually, the available option is blue.` queues **nothing**.
3. State records `latestSpeakable` as the corrected final, `queuedSpeakablePrefix` as the stale red sentence, and `finalQueued:true`.

[remainderAfter](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/ui/src/voice/voice-chat-playback.ts#L185-L207) returns empty when prior text is not a prefix/interior substring; the [consumer](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/ui/src/hooks/useVoiceChat.ts#L2816-L2829) treats that as no remaining speech and marks completion. The original plan must specify a non-monotonic stream contract, not only buffer sizes. Do not blindly replay the full final (duplicates already spoken words); distinguish queued-but-unplayed text, actual played content, and replacement/correction events. Reject unsupported rewrites explicitly or deliver a deliberate corrected utterance with clear ownership.

Second actual probe: `Hello there.` → final `Note: Hello there. More.` queues only `Hello there.` and `More.`. Interior-substring recovery drops `Note:` but records the whole final as queued. Remove silent interior matching; acceptance must compare the actual delivered text sequence against the authorized append/revision contract.

These are deterministic boundary counterexamples, not proof that every production provider rewrites text. Current shell [provisional-frame suppression](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/ui/src/components/shell/useShellVoiceOutput.ts#L175-L186) specifically protects one known wholesale-replacement path and must remain. Other callers, direct hook use, and non-provisional replacement still require a defined contract.

### P2 — Monotonic text alone does not make chunk boundaries pronounceable (reproduced)

Actual callback probe: partial `I am checking the international` followed by final `I am checking the internationalization settings.` queues two independent requests: `I am checking the international` and `ization settings.`. The [threshold branch](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/ui/src/hooks/useVoiceChat.ts#L2831-L2842) sends the entire partial string once it exceeds 24 characters, even when the final word may still be streaming. The debounce flush has the same unresolved trailing-word problem at lines 2669–2706. This is an exact request segmentation defect; no specific acoustic measurement is claimed.

Amend prefetch work to retain an unfinished lexical suffix until a stable delimiter or final event, with language-aware handling where spaces are not word boundaries. A timer does not prove word completion. Preserve all characters and ordering; do not use a maximum-length truncation to repair prosody. Test token streams split inside words, Unicode graphemes, decimal numbers, abbreviations and URLs, then inspect real spoken continuity on supported targets.

### P2 — Latency improvement must separate synthesis scheduling from playback completion

The [worker](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/ui/src/hooks/useVoiceChat.ts#L2382-L2532) awaits each provider's full speak operation. [Decoded playback](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/ui/src/voice/voice-chat-audio-playback.ts#L130-L168) resolves on completion/timeout. Thus a later clip is synthesized only after earlier playback finishes on the buffered local/ElevenLabs path; faster segmentation alone cannot hide that synthesis interval. Implement bounded prefetch with one ordered playback owner and cancelable generation. Bound retained audio bytes/concurrency, not text completeness.

### Examined protections, ownership and acceptance amendments

Decoded playback checks generation both before and after asynchronous decode (`voice-chat-audio-playback.ts` lines 65–67); do not allege a missing decode cancellation guard. `cancelPlayback` increments generation, clears queue, aborts active fetch, and completes the playback waiter; retain all four when prefetch adds multiple requests. Reject late prefetched audio for old generations and test cancellation during synthesis, decode, and playback. Provider failure already fails closed. Coordinate the queue configuration/key race with #30680 so prefetch cannot synthesize one voice and label/cache another.

The shell message watcher explicitly exits for Cartesia realtime (`useShellVoiceOutput.ts` lines 147–151). This report's buffered-path findings must not be presented as a diagnosis of realtime Sonic. Live GitHub inspection confirms #29492 remains OPEN/DRAFT at `b209c79fe2ac1bde176204f078834f9352b8395c`; reusing its work requires exact-head review, not assuming it is merged. HEAD's #30723 changes native HTTP stream metadata validation; it does not repair these queue/text boundaries.

Require evidence for the exact target/provider reproducing the user's symptom: full authorized text vs queued/synthesized/played intervals, first-audio time, inter-clip silence, final-frame arrival, cancellation outcome, and subjective playback review. Pure task-capture probes above establish text loss/splitting but cannot establish acoustic latency or native playback success.

### Independent long-reply finding and repair in progress

The human listening acceptance above applies to the exact short recordings. A separate live navigation test exposed a longer reply ending mid-sentence: 180 words of generated text produced 22.6 seconds of Kokoro audio, and independent ASR found only 87 spoken words. The standalone scheduler passed the entire reply as one phrase; the native Kokoro tokenizer silently retained only its first 510 phoneme tokens.

The repair preflights every segment of the complete utterance before synthesis, splits at word boundaries while preserving ordered text, rejects an indivisible oversized word before emitting a prefix, and sends the same checked IPA to the native ABI v14+ IPA entry. Old libraries without that entry and exhausted audio allocations return explicit errors. Cancellation prevents later segment dispatch.

The exact captured reply now produces 43.875 seconds of real Kokoro audio (SHA-256 `4f335c87ec0087d0c33a79f92df4c94ff26d6c2e279a6ba42bb5eb080f2806ab`). Independent native CPU Qwen3-ASR 0.6B transcription covered every feature section and the exact final sentence, “Tell me what you want to write down first.” Minor ASR wording and punctuation differences remain. The full inference suite passed 2,916 tests across 282 files plus 60 native harness tests; 19 tests were explicitly skipped. Typecheck and lint passed. Independent review then found a separator-only suffix could produce empty IPA after a valid prefix; follow-up `9564979b97` rejects it during complete preflight, with 29 focused tests passing. Follow-up independent review found no remaining actionable defect and independently passed all 29 boundary tests plus the installed-phonemizer adversarial probe. Final root validation remains pending. This is recorded-audio proof, not microphone or all-provider acceptance.

The shell failure/retry recording, desktop/mobile captures, exact human-reviewed clips, and actual application audio are [attached inline](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/issues/30679#issuecomment-5557739959). The native macOS file picker resolved the browser upload failure without changing extension permissions. The MP4 uses explanatory narration; actual application speech is attached separately.


The complete repaired long reply is available as [the original 43.875-second WAV](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31876611/long-reply-complete.wav), SHA-256 `4f335c87ec0087d0c33a79f92df4c94ff26d6c2e279a6ba42bb5eb080f2806ab`. 82:Tfbc,## Problem

Eliza app subscriptions and subscriptions sold by hosted apps need independent customers, entitlements, trials, invoices, and infrastructure funding. The current organization-wide subscription model and product-specific hosted-app bridge cannot provide that contract. Customers must be able to use and buy a hosted app without buying an Eliza app subscription.

## Implementation scope

Extend the existing subscription authority, command journal, event receipts, and allowance ledger into one generic service. Retain Cloud organizations as infrastructure cost accounts. Give app customers a distinct app-scoped billing account, merchant binding, immutable product/plan revision, subscription, entitlement, and usage allowance. All currently eligible Cloud-managed plans receive a seven-day first trial. Reuse app registration, consent, credentials, and revocation.

The Eliza app and Outreachr must consume the generic APIs. Product branding, plan names/prices, workspace business rules, and deployed registration data belong in the respective app, not in Cloud runtime special cases. First-party products may share a merchant while retaining separate customer records; third-party merchants use an account-scoped Stripe Connect adapter.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Existing subscription commands/revisions/fences are extended, not replaced by a parallel lifecycle authority.
- [ ] App, merchant/environment, subscriber billing account, and infrastructure payer ownership are enforced at database and API boundaries.
- [ ] One base subscription per app billing account/product family; plan changes preserve subscription and trial identity.
- [ ] Seven-day trial claims cannot reset through duplicate checkout, plan changes, cancellation, or workspace recreation. Trial allowance is noncash and distinct from paid-invoice allowance.
- [ ] Production trial, checkout, portal, update, cancellation, webhook, reconciliation, and deletion flows use durable commands and an atomic lifecycle finalizer. Late workers cannot restore obsolete access.
- [ ] One-time payment fulfillment and existing infrastructure funding remain correct; app revenue never becomes a customer's global Cloud credit balance.
- [ ] Merchant-scoped customer, price, invoice, portal and refund flows work for first-party and connected-account products, including test/live isolation and the pinned Stripe API version.
- [ ] Generic SDK and HTTP APIs support registration/catalog, trial, subscription/entitlement status, checkout/portal, seats, invoices, and usage.
- [ ] Eliza buyer billing, developer app billing configuration, and a separate hosted-app consumer use the same contract.
- [ ] Existing provider identities, cash balances, trial dates, grants, and invoices survive staged migration; historical organization records are classified by original contract, not silently relabeled as Eliza app subscribers.
- [ ] Product-specific hosted-app runtime routes, environment variables, and implementation are removed after coordinated consumer cutover; immutable historical migrations and adoption proof remain intact.

**Describe the bug**

The English UI renders the *names* of 37 translation keys instead of their text. The character editor's unsaved-changes dialog is titled "Unsaved Changes Title" with the body "Unsaved Changes Body"; its counts read "3 Conversation Count" and "2 Post Count"; the computer-use approval overlay's title is "Title", its body "Body", its mode line "Mode Line"; the browser workspace's blocked-frame card says "Frame Blocked Title" / "Frame Blocked Description"; a dialog button reads "Dont Save".

Two things combine on `origin/develop` (`1045297cca`):

1. `packages/ui/src/i18n/index.ts:48` resolves `localized[key] ?? english[key] ?? defaultValue ?? key`, so the catalog value in `locales/en.json` always wins over the `defaultValue` the call site passes. That is by design (the catalog is the source of truth), and `check-i18n.mjs` enforces that every literal key is catalogued.
2. When the catalog was backfilled, these 37 keys were catalogued with their own Title-Cased key name as the value — `"charactereditor.UnsavedChangesTitle": "Unsaved Changes Title"` — while every call site passes the real English as `defaultValue`. Because of (1), the real English never renders.

```

computeruseapprovaloverlay.ModeLine  "Approval mode: {{mode}}." (mode: "auto")
                                                       ->  "Mode Line"

```

In the app: open the character editor, edit any field, switch character — the dialog is titled "Unsaved Changes Title". Trigger a computer-use approval — the overlay is titled "Title".

Scan of every literal `t("key", { defaultValue: "…" })` call site under `packages/ui/src` (4,300 sites) against `en.json`: 37 keys whose catalog value is the key's own name while the call site supplies different text — either a multi-word label degraded to Title Case ("Drag To Reorder", "Dont Save") or a structural name standing in for a sentence or a placeholder-bearing string ("Reset Confirm Body", "Agent Send Warning", "Mode Line").

# Risks

Medium: introduces a credential-bearing API boundary and a separate product's Stripe operations. Routes require a registered app and hashed client secret. User delegation is short-lived, revocable, and checked against primary account authority; Google ownership remains enforced by the managed connector service. Billing validates app/workspace/customer/price metadata and verifies Stripe webhook signatures. All new routes remain unavailable until explicit Outreachr bindings are configured.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Outreachr can exchange its existing app-login code for scoped identity and managed Google access without copying Google credentials into the CRM. The primary database retains an authorization-code digest so replay stays blocked even after grant revocation or a stale cache read. Google transport permits only the Gmail/calendar operations used by the CRM.

The billing boundary reuses Cloud's Stripe service for separate Outreachr workspace customers and monthly seat prices. Stable idempotency keys protect customer and checkout creation; current subscriptions are read from Stripe and webhooks are signature-verified. Existing Cloud products and subscriptions are not changed.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature; additive backend routes and an append-only delegation migration.

# Documentation changes needed?

Deployment bindings and migration order are documented in the companion Outreachr cloud README and implementation plan. Apply `0376_outreachr_delegations.sql` before enabling the routes; configure the exact app ID/origin/client-secret digest plus Sol/Astra price IDs and a dedicated webhook secret. Use the standard staging certification and production approval workflow.

`outreachr-delegation.test.ts`, `outreachr-billing.test.ts`, and `outreachr-delegations-migration.pglite.test.ts` under `packages/cloud/shared/src`.

Adds the private Agent filesystem boundary needed to stage an exact restore-v3 candidate for #20726. The implementation is split into authority/control, durable JSON, payload, and tree proof/cleanup modules behind one small facade.

This PR does not materialize PGlite/character/media/state/vault components, boot a candidate, publish activation, or route traffic.

## Guarantees

- production is Linux-only and descriptor-bound through `/proc/self/fd`; every traversed directory is opened `O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW`
- one persistent kernel `flock` remains bound to the attempt-root inode across pathname rename
- payload owner/receipt sidecars allow exact crash and lost-response replay without persisting the owner token itself
- canonical durable JSON uses no-replace link publication plus parent-directory fsync and exact crash repair
- payloads reject symlinks, hardlinks, overflow, replaced inodes, and other owners; provider-owned buffers/descriptors are disposed on late abort
- canonical JSON rejects sparse arrays, accessors, symbol keys, and undeclared properties
- cleanup preflights the bounded tree and uses an internal cleanup deadline
- non-Linux pathname emulation is available only with the explicit test-only flag under `NODE_ENV=test`; production fails closed

## Explicit platform limit

`flock` is advisory for cooperative participants. Node does not expose the full `openat2`/`unlinkat`/`linkat(AT_EMPTY_PATH)` set used to eliminate every last-component race against a deliberately non-cooperative same-UID process. Ancestors remain descriptor-bound/no-follow and final identities are revalidated; deployments must keep the staging root private to this Agent authority.

8e:T1b8b,feat(core): durable per-principal capability grants, slice 1 (#23102)

## Summary

First implementation slice for #23102 per the issue's own slicing guidance: a durable subject × capability × resource grant store and the canonical fail-closed `authorizeCapability` decision path, in a new `packages/core/src/features/capabilities/` module. Storage lives in a dedicated `capabilities` Postgres schema, self-materialized through idempotent DDL on first store use (the TrajectoriesService pattern) because no registered plugin carries a schema-bearing entry — relying on plugin-schema migration would leave the tables uncreated in real deployments.

- **Typed, versioned vocabulary** (`types.ts`): canonical subjects (`entity:<uuid>`, `role:<name>`, `world:<uuid>`, case-folded), dot-separated lowercase capabilities, strict selector grammar (`*`, exact ids, trailing `/*` only — printable ASCII allowlist, no leading/trailing/double slashes, length cap). Malformed input is rejected at the write (error-policy J3); legacy rows that drift are quarantined — visible for management, never authoritative.
- **Store** (`CapabilityGrantStore.ts`): validated create, version-checked update, idempotent revoke — each mutation and its global `capability_epoch` bump commit in ONE transaction; a missing epoch singleton rolls the mutation back instead of fabricating progress. Uncapped live-grant reads filtered (expiry `> now`, non-revoked) in SQL. Concurrent-safe promise-memoized DDL bootstrap.
- **Decision path** (`authorizeCapability.ts`): fixed evaluation order — validate (fail closed) → explicit deny grants → allow grants (constraints intersected: numeric min, typed scalar array intersection, structural equality; incompatible → deny) → role-tier composition hook → deny `NO_MATCHING_GRANT` (no implicit allow). No decision cache, so revocation is effective before the next call returns by construction. Every decision attempts exactly one audit row (id generated up front); audit failures are reported through an injected `onAuditFailure` hook (J7; wire to `runtime.reportError` at the boundary) and can never block or flip a decision. Audit rows carry categorical/sanitized fields only — raw malformed values and driver errors never enter the log.
- **Enforcement inventory** (`capability-boundary-inventory.ts`): 12 privileged boundaries (message send/read, device, fs read/write, PTy, git, media read/write, provider invoke, admin API, coding environments) with per-boundary status; the shape is test-validated. Completeness against future repo boundaries is a human-review obligation until the slice-2 classifier.
- Exported node-only from `index.node.ts` (SQL-bound; browser/edge untouched).

## Test evidence

`bun run --cwd packages/core test` scope: **41/41 passing** real-PGlite tests in `CapabilityGrantStore.test.ts` (default vitest lane; PGlite disk data dirs, real Drizzle queries, no mocks of the system under test):

- Self-migration from an empty database; concurrent first calls share one bootstrap
- Restart survival: handle closed, fresh handle opened on the SAME disk dir — grants (and deny grants) created under the first handle remain authoritative; epoch identical
- Revocation visible to the very next decision; expiry boundary `expiresAt <= now` never matches
- Deny-wins over simultaneous allows and over the role tier; role tier never rescues a deny; broken resolver degrades to deny
- Fail-closed: malformed subject/capability/agentId/resource/worldId → `INVALID_REQUEST`; store down → `STORE_UNAVAILABLE`; no grant → `NO_MATCHING_GRANT`
- Audit: per-decision rows, categorical details (raw values withheld), 512-char resource truncation, failure reported through the hook, throwing reporter cannot abort any decision path
- Optimistic-version conflicts; partial unique index (world-aware via nil-uuid coalescing) blocks duplicate active policies and frees on revoke; identical policies legal in distinct worlds and alongside global
- Typed constraint intersection incl. non-scalar arrays → incompatible; nearest expiry across multiple allows
- Quarantine of legacy rows with malformed selector/issuer/capability/subject/effect/provenance
- Mutation rollback when the epoch singleton is missing (zero grant rows survive)
- Boundary inventory shape validation

Typecheck clean (`bun run --cwd packages/core typecheck`), Biome clean, `bun run --cwd packages/core build` succeeds and the built barrel exports `authorizeCapability` + store API (verified by import probe against the built output).

## What does this PR do?

Implements the first production slice of #23103:

1. **Pin/unpin/list through service + REST + agent action.** `DocumentService.setDocumentPinned` performs a CAS-protected metadata mutation through the existing authorization + revision fencing plus the dedicated `expectedPinned` pin-bit fence (review r1: two racing pin writers from the same observed state now serialize — exactly one `updated`, the loser gets a typed conflict and the service's bounded retry converges against fresh state; no second write path). REST: `POST /api/documents/:id/pin` / `DELETE /api/documents/:id/pin` behind the existing mutate gate, mapping typed `DOCUMENT_PIN_UNSUPPORTED` to 503. Agent surface: `pin`/`unpin` subactions on the DOCUMENT umbrella action. The presented-document wire shape now carries `pinned`, and the Documents view shows a visible per-row pending state with a fail-closed unsupported-adapter signal.
2. **Post-#24134 prompt-integrity policy on pinned provider injection.** The deterministic 8,000-token pinned-injection cap (first-N selection + `[PINNED KNOWLEDGE TRUNCATED]` marker) is gone: every authorized selected pinned document reaches the model completely. Provider composition exhausts pagination before selecting pinned documents.

**Coordination with upstream #26780/#28112:** during review, upstream landed prompt-integrity work touching the same provider seam (`renderPinnedDocuments` now returns `{text, truncated: boolean, includedIds}` and callers expose `pinnedDocumentsTruncated` as the completeness signal, always `false`). This branch concedes that seam wholesale to upstream (100% upstream bytes for `provider.ts` + its two test files) and keeps the complete-injection policy through upstream's own shape. An independent integration review (round 5) verified no silent cap/clip/marker remains, no semantic conflict with #28112's rewritten limit semantics in the auto-merged files, and that no required deliverable was dropped.

Explicit non-goals (follow-up slices of #23103): durable entitlement grants/sharing flows (#23102 coordination), multi-room pin scoping UI.

## What kind of change is this?

Features (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require a change to the project documentation. (The plugin-documents `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` pair is updated in-branch for the new pin routes.)

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

`packages/core/src/features/documents/__tests__/actions-pin.test.ts` (agent action wiring), then `plugins/plugin-documents/src/routes.pin.test.ts` (REST + 503 mapping), then `plugins/plugin-inmemorydb/document-pin.test.ts` + `plugins/plugin-sql/src/__tests__/integration/document-pin.real.test.ts` (real adapter persistence, CAS + concurrency).

## Detailed testing steps

- Pin/unpin via the DOCUMENT umbrella action; assert metadata-only mutation through existing authorization (never a second write path).
- `POST /api/documents/:id/pin` on a legacy adapter (inherited base method) — expect 503 typed `DOCUMENT_PIN_UNSUPPORTED`, never a fabricated success.
- Concurrent pin toggles on the same document — REAL two-writer SQL proof on PGlite (`document-pin.real.test.ts`): both writers read before either writes, race `Promise.all` CAS writes; exactly one `updated` + one `conflict`, and the loser's retry against fresh state converges. RED control: removing the `expectedPinned` fence makes both writers report `updated` (lost update) and the test fails.
- Pinned provider injection renders complete content (no budget, no marker).

91:T54a7,On `develop`, a caller cannot trust complete-retrieval traversal. A document request whose vector recall is empty still comes back carrying keyword-corpus rows that never matched the query. A `plugin-inmemorydb` traversal keeps re-serving page one and then rejects a healthy source. A growing-prefix PII walk aborts a stable source with `ElizaError: PII context memories source changed during traversal`.

Those are the failure classes @lalalune reproduced in #25150. Verbatim:

> 1. Hybrid document search can add irrelevant keyword-corpus rows when vector results are empty or sparse.
> 2. The first-party plugin-inmemorydb adapter does not honor the widened stable offset contract, so complete traversal repeats the first page and rejects healthy sources.
> 3. Growing-prefix PII traversal reranks each prefix with BM25, so a stable source can appear unstable as corpus statistics change.
> 4. Deterministic overlapping document pages can pass double-scan equality while duplicating one row and omitting another.
> 5. Requiring two whole-corpus scans to match rejects ordinary concurrent prepends/appends instead of traversing a stable keyset snapshot.

Refs #25150. **This PR does not close it.** It reproduces all five classes as failing tests and makes them pass, but a CHANGES_REQUESTED review found six defects — four P1 — in the fix itself, and none of them are fixed yet. The per-item dispositions are below; every one is conceded. I am keeping the PR open with the blockers enumerated rather than re-requesting review.

## Review findings — per-item disposition

Against [`startrack3r`'s CHANGES_REQUESTED review](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/pull/28336#pullrequestreview-5016829589) (static review of `9197af5`). I re-read each cited location at `d4b8d5a`. **All six still stand. All six are conceded. None are fixed.**

**1. [P1] RLS principal is bound to a result filter — CONCEDED, OPEN.** `plugins/plugin-sql/src/base.ts:4043` still reads `return this.withEntityContext(params.entityId ?? null, async (tx) => {` inside `searchMemoriesPage`, while `params.entityId` is applied separately as a row filter at the `eq(memoryTable.entityId, params.entityId)` condition. The requester principal is `params.accessContext?.requesterEntityId`. Under PostgreSQL RLS this makes a row filter drive `current_entity_id()`, and an omitted filter supplies no principal at all. The reviewer is also right that the existing real-SQL test uses one UUID for both roles and therefore cannot catch it. Fix owed: bind `withEntityContext` to the validated requester with an explicit absent-context policy, plus real-Postgres cases where requester A filters entity B and where the context is missing or empty.

**2. [P1] Shared in-memory storage is not agent-isolated — CONCEDED, OPEN.** `plugins/plugin-inmemorydb/adapter.ts:1375` `searchMemoriesPage` filters on `tableName`, `roomId`, `worldId`, `entityId`, and `unique`, with no `memory.agentId === this.agentId` predicate. The plugin shares one `MemoryStorage` across adapters and the dimension rebuild loads every stored agent into the index, and the PII path calls this without an `AccessContext`. Another agent's rows can therefore reach the result, the count, and the snapshot fingerprint. Fix owed: enforce the agent boundary in both the stable and legacy paths, scope index rebuild per agent, and test two adapters sharing one storage across a rebuild.

**3. [P1] This is not storage-level keyset paging — CONCEDED, OPEN, and it is the acceptance criterion.** Confirmed at head: `searchMemoriesPage` issues `.orderBy(asc(distance), desc(memoryTable.createdAt), desc(memoryTable.id))` with no cursor predicate and no `LIMIT`, then filters, maps, and hands the complete ordered corpus to `createStableRetrievalPage`, which slices and fingerprints it in JavaScript. The two document queries do the same. Every page is O(N) transfer, sort, and hash; a traversal is O(N × pages). The prior body disclosed this as a "tradeoff" in *Scope and risk* while ticking the adapter-keyset acceptance box in the same document — that contradiction is withdrawn and the box is now unticked. Fix owed: push the exclusive `(score, createdAt, id)` continuation and the snapshot fence into each adapter query with `LIMIT pageSize + 1`, plus query-shape and large-corpus assertions.

**4. [P1] Torn in-memory storage/index state — CONCEDED, OPEN.** I confirmed at head that `searchMemoriesPage` guards only with `withDocumentMutationLock`, which chains on `documentMutationTail` (`plugins/plugin-inmemorydb/adapter.ts:872`). The reviewer's point stands: ordinary create/update/delete write storage and the vector index as separate awaited operations outside that tail, and clearing an embedding leaves the HNSW node behind — I have not independently re-derived that second half. A page can rank against stale vector state, return a differently-shaped stored row, and still mint a snapshot over it. Fix owed: serialize those mutations against stable reads (or publish an atomic immutable snapshot), drop the index node when an embedding is cleared, and add forced-interleaving regressions.

**5. Backward-compatibility regressions — CONCEDED, OPEN, both halves.** (a) `plugins/plugin-inmemorydb/adapter.ts:1320` still has `const threshold = params.match_threshold ?? -1;` on the legacy `searchMemories` path, changing the omitted-threshold default from `0.5` and handing existing callers low- and negative-similarity rows. Restoring `0.5` with tests for omitted / explicit `0` / explicit `-1` is owed. (b) `packages/core/src/types/runtime.ts:644,647` declare `searchMemoriesPage` and `rerankMemories` as required `IAgentRuntime` members while the runtime feature-detects them as optional — that breaks structurally typed third-party runtimes. Owed: model them as optional or versioned capability members, or move them to an extended interface.

**6. Stable-helper cross-adapter gaps — CONCEDED, OPEN.** Confirmed at head in `packages/core/src/database/stable-retrieval.ts`: `buildSnapshot` compares `key.id > upperId` as a raw case-sensitive string while the canonical adapter comparator lowercases to match PostgreSQL, and `fingerprint()` hashes only `id`, `createdAt`, `similarity`, `content`, `embedding`, `metadata`, `roomId`, `worldId`, `entityId` — so a mutation to a returned field it omits, such as `unique`, passes the old snapshot unchanged. Owed: canonicalize UUID comparison and duplicate identity, fingerprint the complete canonical returned row, and add parity/mutation tests.

**7. Overstated end-to-end claim — CONCEDED and corrected here.** The reviewer is right that the projection case is not the real end-to-end path the previous body advertised. `packages/core/src/security/issue-25150-runtime-adversarial.test.ts:124` constructs a real `DocumentService`, but the adapter beneath it is `queryDocumentFragments: vi.fn(async () => fragments)` over 1,205 synthetic rows, with a mocked runtime around it. It proves the projection seam does not silently truncate; it does not prove a real DocumentService → storage → planner path. The "real `DocumentService` → projection → `AgentRuntime` dispatch" wording is withdrawn.

**8. Evidence-row markers — FIXED.** All seven mandatory evidence-row markers plus the OCR row were missing from the previous body and are restored below, and the evidence-head marker now carries `d4b8d5a`.

**9. Rebase onto live `develop` — PARTIALLY DONE.** Rebased onto `f2ccf25` at `d4b8d5a`, preserving both sides of the `plugin-inmemorydb` conflict with #28112 (`const limit = params.count ?? params.limit;` from develop, `const threshold = params.match_threshold ?? -1;` from this PR — and per finding 5 that second line is itself owed a revert). `develop` has since advanced 6 commits; another rebase is owed.

## Scope and risk

Risk: medium, and higher than the previous body admitted. `IDatabaseAdapter` / `IAgentRuntime` gain stable-page methods and a capability marker; findings 1, 2 and 5 mean the current shape of those additions changes an authorization principal, crosses an agent boundary, and moves a public default. Legacy adapters take the corrected single-rerank path; first-party adapters take the native contract.

Snapshot verification fingerprints the complete fenced authorized corpus on every page. That makes mutation detection deterministic and is why the tests pass, but it is O(N × pages) over a traversal and is exactly what finding 3 rejects. No scalability improvement is claimed anywhere in this PR.

No documentation change is required: this changes the database/runtime contract and its exported public types, not operator-facing setup.

94:Ta2a,## What changed

- diagnose the exact failed Dedicated canary across its Docker process, Tailscale socket, Headscale REST inventory, tags, route, and active peer identity without exposing private addresses or credentials
- select the unique canonical tailnet IPv4 from Headscale's unordered repeated address field instead of assuming address zero is IPv4
- retain the exact observed Headscale node ID in the replacement cleanup locator before Docker/Headscale address binding, so a mismatch cannot strand an offline peer or poison the next deterministic-name provision
- lock both behaviors with real integration/provider-path regressions

## Why

Fresh signed-in Dedicated canary `33712952322` reached a running agent process and registered an exact tagged Headscale peer, but provisioning still reported missing ingress. Follow-up diagnostics proved the API/CLI peer existed and that its assigned peer address differed from the stale database observation. The provider then dropped the observed node ID when final address binding failed; Docker cleanup proceeded while the Headscale identity remained orphaned.

Headscale's v0.28 node contract exposes `ip_addresses` as a repeated field and does not promise IPv4-first ordering. Treating element zero as the routable IPv4 turns a valid IPv6-first registration into a false registration miss. The repaired selector accepts exactly one canonical CGNAT IPv4 and fails closed on zero or ambiguity.

Closes the remaining registration-settlement and orphan-cleanup defects tracked in #29341.

# Summary

This PR supplies bounded, fail-closed repository-ruleset source and read-only drift tooling. It does not apply a live GitHub control-plane change.

- The former combined manifest is split into disjoint exact-ref `main` and `develop` manifests.
- The main manifest declares its intended active policy; the bounded develop candidate remains mechanically `disabled`.
- The helper requires an explicit manifest, refuses any non-active apply before authentication or API access, validates a serialized in-memory payload, detects ambiguous ownership/effective overlap before and after mutation, and fails closed on semantic readback drift.
- Dry-run performs no GitHub call.
- The readback workflow is external-dispatch only, read-only, bound to the immutable event SHA on exact `refs/heads/develop`, and checks only the active main source manifest. It has no schedule, manual arbitrary-ref trigger, GitHub Environment, Deployment, or apply route.
- Contract tests pin App attribution, absence/null normalization, set-like ordering, unknown fields, array cardinality, post-apply races, redacted diagnostics, and disabled/evaluate refusal.
- Documentation distinguishes source declaration from live effect and records the separate transition/apply/readback/canary gates.

Paid provider calls previously required separate Durable Object requests to acquire a billing lease and mark provider dispatch. This change commits both atomically immediately before provider invocation, removing one network round trip while preserving standing checks, revocation ordering, and durable settlement.

The optimization covers chat completions, messages, embeddings, media generation, voice, MCP/A2A, shared runtime chat, and the generic proxy engine. Standing retains one cache read with asynchronous projection updates and no reread. Provider and dedicated proxy failures include validated trace IDs and sanitized upstream request IDs where available.

Retries reuse a cancellation capability. Both lost acknowledgements and requests that never reach the Durable Object are covered: failures before provider execution settle zero, definitive denials create no lease, and ambiguous release treats only the specific missing-lease response as idempotent. Legacy endpoints remain compatible during rolling deployments.

Validation: focused provider and admission suites passed; API/shared typechecks, 709 mounted route contracts, production Worker dry-run, formatting, and root `bun run verify` passed (376/376 tasks plus repository audits). GitHub run 33979069995 passed every required check for commit 13b9d84028bf0c4a1d402f8919279cf2458091b8, including PostgreSQL authority constraints and billing replay E2E.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Replaces duplicate synchronous/shell Git readers with one complete async reader; uses NUL-delimited filename protocols. A real 10.7 MB change previously lost its final marker while reporting `truncated:false`; Unicode paths previously pointed to nonexistent files.
- Validates analysis document identity and results-map shape before merging. Arrays and mismatched subjects fail without replacing original bytes; arbitrary analyzer IDs are stored as own data properties.
- Disposes the idle worker's abort listener on normal timer expiry and handles already-aborted signals immediately.
- Replaces two 16,000-character event-payload cutoff helpers with a scheduling-owned JSON boundary; persistence, retry/escalation and final prompt assembly retain complete event data. Unsupported data fails before task claim.
- Makes widget execution errors nonzero, clears old output, and reuses local fixture/Tailwind helpers instead of a CDN and fixed wait. Completed widget findings retain the existing `FAIL_ON_VIOLATIONS` policy.
- Moves byte-identical finance/health token encryption into a Node-only shared subpath, retaining plugin compatibility exports and old envelopes.
- Removes 13 unregistered/unexported voice-profile prototype files, including fabricated diarization and a 617-line self-contained role “integration” suite. Live voice-profile persistence remains in local-inference.

## What kind of change is this?

Behavioral bug fixes, consolidation, and removal of unused code. 44 files; net 749 lines removed including tests and compatibility adapters.

# Documentation changes needed?

Updated shared subpath documentation and paired UI CLAUDE/AGENTS instructions. Guide parity passes. The detailed audit and remaining candidates are retained as local review artifacts, not committed evidence.

9c:Te95,
## What this adds

`packages/core/src/messaging/interactions/sessions.ts` exported three surfaces with no test coverage anywhere on `develop`:

- `applyMessageInteractionClaim` — the pure atomic claim transition, including lease acquisition, identical-lease `in_progress`, expired-lease `resumed` with attempt increment, digest comparison against claimed/committed/completed states, preset-response tampering refusal, binding mismatch, revocation/expiry refusal while pending, reference/clock/TTL validation;
- `validateMessageInteractionResponse` — object/array rejection, unexpected-field and missing-required-field (named from schema fields) rejection, boolean/finite-number/UTF-8-byte-limit enforcement, option membership including number-to-string matching, and media-capability URL / byte / MIME validation for attachments;
- `responseSchemaForInteraction` — choice options vs `allowCustom`, text-like byte capping against `maxTextResponseBytes` (non-text fields keep their own bound), secret-field refusal outside the sensitive flow, followups-to-payload mapping, task acknowledgement shape.

The suite also covers the callback encode/decode pair (round-trip plus every malformed shape), the store-level branches not exercised by the existing API-level suite (duplicate-reference collision, clone isolation, double-commit refusal, concurrent claim serialization, `listCommitted` time/limit/ordering, `deleteExpired` per-terminal-state timestamps), and an authority end-to-end run proving exactly-once execution: a second consume of the same replay key replays the retained receipt without re-running the effect executor.

It complements the existing `session-authority.test.ts`, which drives the store and authority APIs; the pure transition functions and validators were previously reachable only through that narrower surface.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Replaces Billing's indefinite signed-out skeleton with an explicit sign-in state wired to the Settings host login flow.
- Distinguishes auth resolution, query pending/error/paused/freshness, unavailable-user, and content states instead of rendering cached data as current.
- Keys invoice cache entries by organization so switching tenants cannot paint the previous organization's invoice.
- Gives sign-in and retry actions agent-operable descriptors and correct busy/disabled behavior.
- Applies the same freshness rules to the invoice detail route.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking).

# Documentation changes needed?

No. This restores the intended runtime contract and adds user-facing strings through the existing i18n catalog.

## What changed

- removes the isolate-local inference refusal map that could reject a healthy request after an asynchronous settlement or projection failure; the revision-aware organization Durable Object remains the admission authority
- removes the duplicate app-settlement balance projection invalidation while preserving fail-closed repair semantics
- adds safe top-level HTTP status evidence and bounded child-failure diagnostics to the latency certification harness
- records browser-literal adoption request and exact provisioning-job lifecycle timing without serializing job identifiers
- preserves the original typed Dedicated provisioning failure cause through retry settlement
- adds trace IDs, phase timing, and structured internal failures to the Dedicated adoption boundary while keeping public errors sanitized

## Why

The paired staging trace isolated a transient 503 to a redundant isolate-local refusal fast path. Warm successful calls showed roughly 74 ms before provider forwarding: about 3 ms standing cache, 25 ms organization rate-limit DO, 26 ms balance lease DO, and 21 ms dispatch marker DO. Cerebras response headers were roughly 75 ms, close to direct calls. This patch removes the incorrect extra authority and makes the remaining Cloudflare, adoption, and provider boundaries directly diagnosable.

# Risk

**Medium.** This changes one-time SSO code custody, exchange finalization, local token publication, cookie synchronization, and logout ordering. A regression could strand a login, publish a stale token, navigate after a superseding exchange, or recreate a session after logout.

The implementation keeps the API contract narrow, serializes same-realm finalization, bounds cookie synchronization, and adds deterministic tests for StrictMode, unmount, state changes, out-of-order responses, stale persistence, navigation failure, cookie ordering, and logout races.

# What does this PR do?

It hardens both legs of the cloud SSO bridge.

1. **Abandoned mint custody**
   - Burns a minted one-time code exactly once if the route unmounts, changes authorization state, or cannot hand off.
   - Adds a sessionless, destruction-only `POST /burn` endpoint restricted to exact bridge origins.
   - Keeps successful handoff and StrictMode replay single-shot.

2. **Generation-safe exchange and recovery**
   - Consumes state/verifier once and ignores late results from superseded route generations.
   - Prevents stale exchanges from publishing a token or navigating.
   - Serializes token publication and server-cookie synchronization so the newest valid exchange wins.
   - Makes cookie synchronization abortable and bounded to 10 seconds.
   - Orders logout/account-switch teardown with exchange finalization and prevents any session POST from starting after a concurrent logout.
   - Recovers from rejected bridge redirects instead of leaving the app or join page on a permanent spinner.

The same-realm browser contract is covered. Cross-tab/cross-realm coordination is not claimed; the generation queue, abort controller, and logout epoch are module-local.

# Review guide

Start with:

- `packages/ui/src/cloud/sso-bridge/SsoBridgeRoute.tsx`
- `packages/ui/src/cloud/sso-bridge/sso-bridge.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/steward-session-client/index.ts`
- Their adjacent tests

Important invariants:

- Before the guarded persistence commit point, a superseded exchange writes and emits nothing.
- Once a valid persistence begins, later valid generations are ordered after it and the newest one wins.
- A stale generation never navigates.
- Logout wins over an exchange still waiting on persistence or cookie synchronization.
- The burn endpoint remains destruction-only and exposes no validity oracle.

ac:T5d8,Fixes #29935

## Summary

- wait for the hosted logout API to confirm durable logout before clearing the browser credential and navigating away
- return a retryable failure when the cross-host logout barrier cannot be persisted
- resolve bearer and environment-scoped cookie credentials once, then use the same verified identity for the logout marker, strong inference cutoff, cache invalidation, session teardown, and audit
- fall back to a valid scoped cookie when a stale local bearer is present

## Root cause

The logout route treated failure to persist the cross-host logout marker as best-effort and still returned success. The UI then cleared its local credential and navigated to login even though the paired origin could immediately restore the surviving session. A stale local bearer could also mask a valid hosted cookie and create a retry loop.

## Verification

- `bun test packages/cloud/api/auth/logout/route.test.ts` (11 passed)
- `bun run --cwd packages/ui test --run src/cloud/sso-bridge/sso-bridge.test.ts --testNamePattern='signOutFromSsoBridgedHost'` (4 passed)
- `bun run --cwd packages/cloud/api typecheck`
- `bun run --cwd packages/cloud/shared typecheck`
- `bun run --cwd packages/ui typecheck`
- `bun run verify`
- two independent adversarial reviews found no remaining release blockers

The deferred-response regression specifically proves that the local credential remains present while hosted logout is pending and is removed only after the server confirms success.
ad:Tae6,## Summary
Fixes #30650.

On hosts with ample memory (such as a 24 GB Apple Silicon Mac), Settings → Models & Providers previously offered `eliza-1-9b` as the default download with an active Download button. However, the canonical catalog and live `/api/local-inference/hub` response mark `eliza-1-9b` as `publishStatus: pending` (only 2B and 4B tiers are published in the Gemma-4 cutover). 

The Settings catalog policy (`isSettingsDefaultLocalModel`) filtered family and hidden flags but ignored publication state, causing `FirstRunOffer` and ladder recommenders to pick an un-cut tier that the download publication boundary subsequently rejects.

## Proposed Changes
1. **Catalog Policy (`catalog-policy.ts`):**
   - Added `isPublishedLocalModel(model: CatalogModel): boolean` checking `(model.publishStatus ?? eliza1TierPublishStatus(model.id as Eliza1TierId)) === "published"`.
   - Updated `isSettingsDefaultLocalModel(model)` to require that the model is published, filtering out pending models from the Settings curated catalog while preserving catalog ordering.
2. **Recommender (`recommendation.ts`):**
   - In `selectRecommendedModelForSlot`, gated ladder candidate eligibility on publication status so high-memory hosts skip pending tiers (such as 9B) and select the next fitting published tier (such as 4B).
   - In `fallbackCandidates`, filtered out non-published models.
3. **FirstRunOffer (`FirstRunOffer.tsx`):**
   - Updated `pickRecommended` to filter fallback candidates by publication state.
   - When no published model is available, `recommended` returns `null`, rendering the distinct unavailable state (`firstrunoffer.detailNoModel`: *"No local chat model is available on this device."*) without rendering an active Download button.
4. **ModelHubView (`ModelHubView.tsx`):**
   - In `ModelHubView`, when no published models exist in the catalog, render a distinct unavailable state banner (`data-testid="model-hub-unavailable"`).
   - Installed models continue to remain accessible via `ActiveModelBar` and installed model surfaces.
5. **Tests:**
   - Updated `catalog-policy.test.ts` to verify that `filterSettingsDefaultLocalModels` excludes pending models (`eliza-1-9b`, `eliza-1-27b`) unless explicitly published, and returns `[]` when all candidates are pending.
   - Added unit test in `catalog.test.ts` demonstrating that a 24 GB Apple Silicon host skips pending `eliza-1-9b` and recommends published `eliza-1-4b`.
   - Added `FirstRunOffer.test.tsx` covering published model recommendation and the distinct unavailable state when no models are published.

- Verified catalog ordering is preserved by `filterSettingsDefaultLocalModels`.

b2:T6a0,## Summary

`packages/cloud/shared/src/db/crypto/remote-host-token.ts` is the only module in `db/crypto/` without a dedicated test suite. The plaintext `rhost_v1_` token is returned once at enrollment (`packages/cloud/api/v1/remote/hosts/route.ts`) and every later lookup authenticates through the persisted `sha256:` digest (`remote-hosts.ts`, `remote-sessions-store.ts`, `remote-command-envelopes.ts`), so a shape, determinism, or guard regression is silent at the consumer boundary and locks out every enrolled remote host after upgrade.

This PR adds a colocated contract-pin suite over the real exported functions (real WebCrypto, no mocks, no database), following the conventions of sibling suites like `remote-pairing-code.test.ts`. No production code changes.

## What the tests pin

- **Mint shape (4 tests):** `rhost_v1_` + exactly 43 base64url chars (no `+`, `/`, or `=` padding leak), distinct across calls, entropy across the full 32-byte range.
- **Digest shape + determinism (5 tests):** `sha256:` + 64 lowercase hex chars, deterministic for the same token, distinct for different tokens, and a fixed-token digest match.
- **Fail-closed rejection (4 tests):** malformed input (empty, wrong-length body, wrong version prefix, non-base64url alphabet) throws `TypeError` instead of persisting a garbage digest that would poison the row.

## Validation

- `bun test src/db/crypto/remote-host-token.test.ts` — 13 pass, 0 fail.
- Mutation spot-checks (drop `sha256:` prefix, `{43}`→`{42}` boundary) go red, confirming the suite detects the regressions it exists to catch.
- Full `src/db/crypto/` directory: 130 pass, 0 fail.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; Biome check clean.

Closes #29596
b3:T80b,## What

Preserves fenced code block contents and indentation losslessly during stage-direction stripping and assistant text spacing tidying in `@elizaos/shared`. Deduplicates `packages/agent/src/api/chat-text-helpers.ts` to re-export the canonical implementation from `@elizaos/shared`.

## Why it matters

Fixes #30590.
`tidyAssistantTextSpacing` previously stripped leading indentation from every line (via `.replace(/\n[ \t]+/g, "\n")`), with no awareness of fenced code blocks. Assistant responses containing code blocks (such as Python, YAML, Makefiles, diffs, list-nested snippets) lost their indentation before reaching the parser, resulting in syntactically broken code.

## Changes

- In `packages/shared/src/utils/assistant-text.ts`:
  - Added `preserveCodeRegions` to shield fenced code blocks behind sentinels before stage-direction stripping and whitespace normalization, and restore them intact afterwards.
  - Anchored code block matching with lookbehind `(?<=^|\n)[ \t]*` to capture opening fence indentation inside the sentinel, ensuring list-nested code blocks (e.g. 4-space bullet items) retain symmetrical indentation and CommonMark fence termination.
  - Used an underscore-free and asterisk-free sentinel (`\u0000ELIZACODE<n>\u0000`) to eliminate collisions with stage direction formatting passes.
- In `packages/agent/src/api/chat-text-helpers.ts`:
  - Deduplicated the local implementation and re-exported `stripAssistantStageDirections` from `@elizaos/shared`.
  - **Behavior delta**: Converges the agent onto shared's canonical stage-direction rules (100-character inner cap, ASCII word matching, curly-quote boundary recognition `“‘”’`, and unbounded whitespace quantifiers). Kept the agent's 100k+ character test in `chat-text-helpers.test.ts` as a regression guard.
- Added unit tests in `packages/shared/src/utils/assistant-text.test.ts` and `packages/agent/src/api/chat-text-helpers.test.ts` covering Python indentation, YAML configs, comments containing stage words, streaming code blocks, and list-nested code blocks.b4:Ta89,Closes #30581.

ba:Tb49,## Summary
Warm staging traces show that Cloud inference executes two serialized network round-trips immediately before invoking Cerebras/upstream:
1. Billing admission Durable Object lease (`/lease` or `/lease-authorized`) (~26 ms)
2. Dispatch marker (`/dispatch`) (~21 ms)

This PR resolves #30635 by fusing these two operations into a single durable commit at the provider boundary for `/v1/chat/completions`, eliminating ~21–26 ms of latency per request while preserving complete cancellation, zero-settlement, alarm-recovery, and replay invariants.

---

## Changes
1. **Durable Object (`packages/cloud/api/src/inference-admission-gate.ts`)**:
   - Added `dispatch?: boolean` and `preProviderCancellationToken?: string` to `LeaseRequest` and `AuthorizedLeaseRequest`.
   - In `this.lease()`, atomically persist the lease with `phase: "dispatched"`, `preProviderCancellationToken`, and updated alarm/ledger in one commit when `dispatch: true`.
   - Handled duplicate/replay: if already leased/dispatched, safely update expiry and return `dispatched: true, duplicate: true` without double debit.
   - Preserved pre-provider release capability: `/release` allows releasing a dispatched lease if and only if the valid `preProviderCancellationToken` matches.

2. **Client Service (`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/inference-admission-gate.ts`)**:
   - Added `dispatch?: boolean` to `acquireInferenceAdmissionLease`. Generates `preProviderCancellationToken` and sends it with `dispatch: true`.
   - Updated `markInferenceAdmissionLeaseDispatched`: consumes `preProviderCancellationToken` when already dispatched (zero network round-trip).
   - Updated `releaseInferenceAdmissionLease` & `settleInferenceAdmissionLease`: allows zero-settlement release using `preProviderCancellationToken` if upstream aborted before provider call.

3. **Organization Admission (`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/organization-inference-admission.ts`)**:
   - Added `dispatch?: boolean` to `OrganizationInferenceAdmissionParams` and forwarded to `acquireInferenceAdmissionLease`.

4. **Completions Route (`packages/cloud/api/v1/chat/completions/route.ts`)**:
   - Passed `dispatch: true` to `admitOrganizationInference` so the initial admission gate combines lease + dispatch before calling the upstream provider.

---

bc:T1a29,# What

`RemoteTargetDesktopService.resumeEligibleLoopback` decides whether a desktop may resume acting as a **remote-control target** after a restart. Its docstring makes a fail-closed promise:

> Missing/corrupt credential or journal state never degrades into a fresh enrollment or an unpinned runner.

Nothing asserted it. The two suites in this directory cover the runner and the same-host integration path, not this decision. This adds 20 tests. No production change.

# The decision table

| vault | active sessions | staged sessions | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| not enrolled | ≥1 | — | **throws** |
| not enrolled | 0 | — | `not_enrolled`, runner stopped |
| enrolled | ≥1 | — | `active_authority`, runner **running** |
| enrolled | 0 | ≥1 (unresolved) | `activation_recovery`, runner **running** |
| enrolled | 0 | 0 | `no_active_authority`, runner stopped |

The throw is the one that matters. Returning `not_enrolled` there would look like a clean first run and invite a fresh enrollment, quietly orphaning a controller grant that is still live in the journal. That substitution is now a failing mutant.

Every clause of the active-authority filter is covered individually — not staged, not stopped, not revoked, not expired — including that **expiry is inclusive** (`expiresAt >= now`), so a grant expiring exactly now still counts rather than dying a millisecond early on every restart.

And `resumed: false` is asserted to also mean *not running*, via `service.status()`. A runner started on a "no authority" path would poll the relay for commands with nothing backing it.

# I got the staged-activation contract wrong first, and the failures corrected me

My initial tests assumed a staged session simply yields `activation_recovery`. It doesn't. `resumeEligibleLoopback` calls `recoverStagedActivations()` **before** reading the decision, so the answer depends on what the relay says:

| relay response to `commitActivation` | journal effect | resume outcome |
|---|---|---|
| success | session promoted to `active` | `active_authority` |
| 404 / 409 / 410 (grant gone) | session **deleted** | `no_active_authority` |
| 0 / 408 / 429 / 5xx (outage) | stays `staged` | `activation_recovery` |
| anything else (e.g. 403) | — | **propagates** |

So **a relay outage is the only path to `activation_recovery`** — the runner comes up to keep retrying rather than either discarding a real grant or claiming authority it hasn't confirmed. That's a genuinely nice piece of design and it now has tests that say so. All four rows are asserted, including that a 403 is neither "gone" nor "offline" and must not be silently classified as either.

Also asserted: a stopped or revoked staged session is **never committed at all** (`commitActivation` not called), and recovery is skipped entirely when the vault isn't enrolled.

# Mutation testing: 18 mutants, 18 killed

Across `remote-target-rpc.ts` and `remote-target-runner.ts`:

- the fail-closed throw replaced with `not_enrolled`
- each of the four active-filter clauses dropped individually
- `expiresAt >= now` → `>`, and expiry ignored entirely
- both staged-filter clauses dropped
- `activation_recovery` relabelled `active_authority`
- recovery run when not enrolled, and recovery skipped entirely
- runner started on `no_active_authority` and on `not_enrolled`; runner *not* started on `active_authority`
- `410` dropped from the gone set; `5xx` dropped from the transient set; the unclassified-error rethrow turned into `continue`
- the staged commit filter ignoring `revokedAt`

One of these needed a second pass. "Runner started on `no_active_authority`" initially survived because I was only asserting that `claimNext` hadn't been called — too indirect. Switching to `service.status()` killed it and two more lifecycle mutants I added afterwards.

# A red herring I checked before reporting

`remote-target-runner.test.ts` shows **2 failures under a bare `bun test`** on unmodified `develop`. That is a wrong-runner artifact, not a defect: this directory has its own `vitest.electrobun.config.ts`, and under that config it is **39 pass / 0 fail**. Worth knowing if anyone else runs into it.

bd:T56b,## Summary

- On cloud-staging (`cloud-staging.eliza.app`), the in-app browser workspace's `GET /api/browser-workspace` returned 404 because the shared-agent catch-all adapter didn't handle the path
- This caused the `BrowserWorkspaceView` to show a persistent red error banner (`setLoadError`) with "Not found" on every load
- Clicking the "+" new tab button also hit a 404, silently failing

**Root cause:** The shared-agent route adapter in `v1/eliza/agents/[agentId]/api/[...path]/route.ts` only handles specific shell paths and 404s everything else. `browser-workspace` was not listed.

**Fix:** Add the same graceful stubs the local agent server uses when `plugin-browser` is absent:
- `GET /api/browser-workspace` → `{ mode: "web", tabs: [] }` (200) — workspace loads in its designed-empty state, no error banner
- `POST /api/browser-workspace/tabs`, `/command`, and tab mutations → 503 "Browser workspace is not available on this platform" — shows a clear error toast when the user clicks "+" to open a tab

## Test plan

- [ ] On `cloud-staging.eliza.app`, navigate to the Browser tab — the workspace should load empty with no red error banner
- [ ] Click "+" to open a new tab — should show an error toast "Browser workspace is not available on this platform" instead of failing silently with a 404

c0:Ta25,## Summary
Fixes #30646.

In `packages/app-core/platforms/electrobun/src/index.ts`, the external-runtime branch in `main()` previously only injected the API base and bypassed `_startAgent()`. Because `_startAgent()` was skipped, the native loopback session handshake (`primeDesktopSessionAuth`) and subsequent renderer reload (`reloadRendererAfterDesktopSessionPrime`) never executed for external development runtimes like `bun run dev:desktop --cloud-target=offline`. As a result, no `eliza_session` or `eliza_csrf` cookies were installed into the Electrobun webview cookie jar, causing subsequent renderer requests (such as `POST /api/first-run`, notifications, and model configurations) to return 401 Unauthorized.

## Changes
1. **Export loopback validator**:
   - Export `isLoopbackBase` from `packages/app-core/platforms/electrobun/src/native/auth-bridge.ts`.
2. **Invoke agent lifecycle for external runtimes**:
   - In `main()`, invoke `_startAgent()` when `rt.mode === "external" || rt.mode === "local"`.
3. **Initialize loopback external runtime session**:
   - In `_startAgent()`, check whether `externalApiBase` is a loopback address using `isLoopbackBase(externalApiBase)`.
   - For external loopback runtimes, resolve `rendererBase` (accounting for Vite/dev-server loopback origin), prime the session via `primeDesktopSessionAuth(externalApiBase, rendererBase)`, publish the renderer-facing API base and token, set agent ready, and reload the renderer via `reloadRendererAfterDesktopSessionPrime`.
4. **Preserve remote runtime isolation & fail-closed invariants**:
   - Remote (non-loopback) external runtimes are strictly excluded from local session priming and never receive locally minted authority.
   - Failed handshakes fail closed, leaving the renderer in the standard unauthenticated/login state.
5. **Unit test coverage**:
   - Added tests in `desktop-session-prime.test.ts` verifying:
     - External loopback runtime primes authority across both API base and dev-server renderer origin.
     - Remote external runtimes are distinguished and excluded by `isLoopbackBase`.
     - Failed handshake produces no cookies and fails closed.

# Risks

Low. The change is confined to one pure string-transform helper
(`stripThinkingParameters`) inside `plugins/plugin-anthropic-proxy`'s forward
request pipeline. It only widens comma consumption so removal of the top-level
`thinking` parameter never leaves a dangling separator. `thinkingParamsStripped`
stays exactly `1` per stripped parameter, so downstream stats are unchanged, and
the mid/last/sole-key behavior is byte-for-byte identical to before (proven by
the existing suite staying green and by the new position-invariance cases).

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Fixes a data-integrity bug on the Anthropic proxy's core body-rewrite path. The
forward pipeline strips the top-level `thinking` parameter before forwarding the
request to `api.anthropic.com`. `stripThinkingParameters` removed
`"thinking":{...}` but only consumed a **leading** comma. When `thinking` is the
**first** key of the top-level object there is no leading comma, so the trailing
comma was left behind, producing malformed JSON such as `{,"system":...}`.
Anthropic rejects that body with `400 invalid JSON`, silently breaking every
extended-thinking request whose serialization happens to place `thinking` first.

This occurs in production whenever the request already carries a `system` array
(array form, used for prompt caching) **and** `metadata` (user_id): neither the
billing nor the metadata injector prepends a key ahead of `thinking`, so it
stays the first key and the corruption reaches the wire.

The strip now consumes the leading comma when present, and otherwise (first key)
consumes the trailing comma, so removal never leaves a dangling separator
regardless of the parameter's position.

Following static review, the strip was hardened so it never emits malformed
JSON on any raw client body, not just minified ones: the leading-comma check
now skips insignificant whitespace (so a pretty-printed body with `thinking`
as the last key no longer leaves a trailing comma), and the value boundary is
brace-matched with string/escape tracking via `findMatchingObjectEnd` instead
of the first `}` (so a nested object under `thinking` or a `}` inside a string
value no longer ends removal early and orphans syntax). Three raw-wire
regression cases cover these shapes and fail against the prior source. This is
a deliberate, documented divergence from `proxy.js` v2.2.3's string operations,
noted in the module header so it is not reconciled away as drift.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue).

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require a change to the project documentation. Behavior is
restored to what the pipeline already intended (valid JSON with the `thinking`
param removed); no public surface, env var, or contract changed.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Requires nonblank access and exchange refresh tokens, validates optional rotated refresh tokens, and requires a positive finite expiry.
- Rejects expiry values whose absolute timestamp would overflow to a non-finite value.
- Reports malformed JSON and malformed response shapes as actionable `ElizaError` failures without including token values.
- Adds adversarial exchange and refresh regression coverage, including JSON numeric overflow.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue).

c7:T193b,# The defect

`getTweetWhere` and `getTweetsWhere` sit five lines apart and differ by one keyword:

```ts
// getTweetWhere
const matches = isCallback ? await query(tweet) : checkTweetMatches(tweet, query);

// getTweetsWhere
const matches = isCallback ? query(tweet) : checkTweetMatches(tweet, query);
//                           ^^^^^^^^^^^^ no await
```

`TweetQuery` explicitly permits an async predicate:

```ts
export type TweetQuery =
  | Partial<Tweet>
  | ((tweet: Tweet) => boolean | Promise<boolean>);
```

An unawaited Promise is **always truthy**, so `getTweetsWhere` with an async predicate returns *every* tweet. A filter that silently filters nothing. This is public API — `client.getTweetsWhere` is documented with a usage example in `client.ts`.

I proved it by running it rather than reading it. Three tweets, an async predicate matching two:

```
getTweetsWhere → 1,2,3     ← all of them
getTweetWhere  → 1         ← correct
```

A **rejected** predicate was worse: the rejected Promise is still truthy, so the tweet was kept as a match and the rejection became an unhandled promise rejection instead of surfacing to the caller.

# The fix

Add the `await`, mirroring `getTweetWhere`. Behaviour is unchanged for synchronous predicates.

Reverting only that keyword, with the new tests in place, fails exactly three:

```
× awaits an ASYNC predicate instead of keeping everything
× honours an async predicate that rejects everything
× propagates a rejected predicate rather than dropping the tweet

Tests  3 failed | 19 passed
```

# Tests

`tweets-query.test.ts`, 23 tests, no network — every case drives an in-memory async iterable. None of these functions had any.

**`nextTimelinePageCursor`** is the guard that stops a repeating provider cursor from looping forever. Covered: a terminal `undefined` and a terminal `""` (falsy, so it must not be recorded and then re-reported as a repeat on the next page); an immediate repeat; and the **A → B → A cycle**, which a naive "same as last cursor" check would miss and which loops just as permanently. Also that the error carries `source` and `pageCount` for diagnosis, and that two concurrent runs stay independent through their own `Set`.

**The query helpers**: partial-object matching across multiple keys, sync predicates, async predicates, empty-array vs `null` on no match, stream order preserved, and that `getTweetWhere` **stops consuming the stream** once it has a match (asserted by counting what the generator produced, not by inspecting the result).

Two behaviours pinned as decisions rather than accidents:

- **`checkTweetMatches` compares strictly.** `"0" == 0` is true, so a `==` would let a numeric id from a caller match a string id from the API and silently widen the filter.
- **An empty query object matches everything**, because `Object.keys({}).every(...)` is vacuously true.

# Mutation testing: 12 mutants, 11 killed

Killed: the `await` removed (and separately removed from `getTweetWhere`), the terminal-cursor guard removed and narrowed to `undefined`-only, the repeat guard removed, the cursor recorded before the guard rather than after, `pageCount` dropped from the error context, `every` → `some`, `===` → `==`, `null` → `undefined` on no match, and `getTweetWhere` collecting all matches instead of returning at the first.

**One survivor, and it is provably equivalent.** Re-adding the refused cursor to `seenCursors` before throwing cannot be detected: the only way to reach that throw is for the cursor to *already* be in the Set, so the add is a no-op. No test can distinguish it.

# Recorded, not changed

`getLatestTweet(user, includeRetweets, max, auth)` passes the flag straight through as `{ isRetweet: includeRetweets }`. So `includeRetweets: true` selects **only retweets** rather than "retweets as well", and the `max === 1` shortcut returns the first tweet ignoring the flag entirely. That reads like a naming/semantics mismatch, but changing it would alter what existing callers get back — your call, not mine, so I left it alone and didn't write a test that would freeze it either way.

cb:T892,# Add regression coverage for world-metadata CAS/optimistic-concurrency helpers

## What
Adds a full test suite for `packages/core/src/database/world-metadata-cas.ts`
(previously **zero coverage**, despite being exported on `index.node/browser/edge`
and used by `runtime.ts` + `inMemoryAdapter` for cross-adapter optimistic
concurrency). 26 tests across all 9 exported helpers.

## Why it matters
These helpers protect world metadata against **lost updates** and **stale/late
writes** when multiple adapters or legacy whole-world writers interleave. A
regression here is silent data loss — no crash, just the wrong winner persisting.

## Scope
- `requireFreshWorldMetadataRevision` — stale-write protection (mismatch + malformed fail-closed)
- `mergeWorldMetadataForLegacyWrite` — preserves the adapter-owned revision; **never** lets caller input clobber connector `roles`/`roleSources` authority state
- `advanceWorldMetadataRevision` — invalid / exhausted / no-mutation
- `getWorldMetadataRevision` — absent-default-0, fail-closed on malformed
- `appendWorldMetadataRoleAudit` — init, append, deep-clone, no aliasing
- `worldMetadataValueEquals` — jsonb semantics (key order irrelevant, `undefined` absent, strict types)
- `initializeWorldMetadataRevision` — normalizes to 0

## Verification
Scratch Vitest sandbox against the **real** source: **26/26 pass**.
Sabotage-run proves the tests are load-bearing (each mutation breaks the suite):
- removing the stale-write guard → **1 test fails**
- removing the `leftKeys.length` equality check → **1 test fails**
- weakening the malformed-revision fail-closed → **3 tests fail**

Biome `check` clean (lint gate passed).

# Background

## What does this PR do?

`ScreenCaptureWeb.startRecording()` guards against concurrent recording with `if (this.isRecording) throw new Error("Recording already in progress")`, but `this.isRecording` was only set to `true` **after** the first `await getDisplayMedia(...)`. Two concurrent invocations (or a rapid double-click through the public plugin API) both cleared the guard, both opened the OS screen-share picker, and both acquired display `MediaStream`s. The second call overwrote `this.mediaStream`, orphaning the first stream:

- The first stream's tracks were never `.stop()`'d, so the OS "you are sharing your screen" indicator stayed lit and capture kept running until GC — a resource and privacy leak.
- Both `MediaRecorder`s targeted the shared `this.recordedChunks` buffer, so the orphaned first recorder could corrupt the second recording's data.

The guard's explicit intent to serialize recording was defeated. Prior fleet fixes (#22036 mic-denied leak, #22361 pause-duration) hardened this file but left the entry race unaddressed.

**Fix:** latch a synchronous `starting` flag at the very top of `startRecording`, before any `await`, and clear it in a `finally` that wraps the whole setup body. The guard now checks `this.isRecording || this.starting`, closing the in-flight window. On success `isRecording` is `true` and keeps guarding; on the option-validation throw or the existing J2 rollback rethrow, `isRecording` is back to `false` and the `finally` releases the latch so a subsequent legitimate start still works.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes a resource/privacy leak and data-corruption race).

# Documentation changes needed?

No. Behavior of the public `startRecording` contract is unchanged for correct single-call usage; only the previously-undefined concurrent-call behavior is now the documented "Recording already in progress" rejection the guard always intended.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

`plugins/plugin-native-screencapture/src/web.test.ts` — two new tests exercise the real `startRecording` contract through the existing fake `getDisplayMedia` / `MediaRecorder` / track doubles (no real browser APIs):

1. **Two concurrent `startRecording()` calls** — asserts exactly one rejects with `/already in progress/`, `getDisplayMedia` is called exactly once, only one `MediaRecorder` is constructed, and the single acquired track is not orphaned (not stopped while recording, then stopped on `stopRecording`).
2. **Latch clears after a failed start** — a mic-denied failure runs the J2 rollback; a subsequent `startRecording()` must succeed (proving the `finally` released the `starting` latch rather than wedging the plugin).

## Detailed testing steps

```bash
bun install --minimum-release-age=0   # global bunfig sets a 7-day min release age; override for CI parity
bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-native-screencapture test        # 24 passed (22 existing + 2 new)
bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-native-screencapture typecheck   # clean
bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-native-screencapture lint:check  # clean
```

**Failing-before proof:** running only the fix in `web.ts` reverted (tests present), the concurrent-start test fails with `expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0` — i.e. **zero** rejections and **both** calls acquired a display stream. With the fix, `getDisplayMedia` call count drops 2 → 1 and the second call rejects. See inline logs below.

cd:Ta34,## Summary

`packages/core/src/database.ts` exports the portable pagination and ordering contract that every database adapter and the agent memory browse API rely on, but none of its four exported functions has a direct test. This PR adds a colocated, deterministic suite pinning those contracts. No production code changes.

## Why this contract matters (shipped consumers)

- **`validateQueryEntitiesPagination` / `validateTaskQueryPagination`** are the only rejection path for malformed `limit`/`offset` input at `AgentRuntime.queryEntities` / `AgentRuntime.getTasks` (`runtime.ts`), `InMemoryDatabaseAdapter`, `plugin-sql/src/base.ts`, and `plugin-inmemorydb/adapter.ts`. A regression would let garbage pagination through to every adapter.
- **`compareMemoryIds`** drives keyset cursor decisions in the agent memory browse API (`packages/agent/src/api/memory-routes.ts`, `/api/memory`), the iOS capacitor bridge, and in-memory adapter ordering. It matches PostgreSQL `uuid` ordering (case-normalized) — a regression here silently skips or repeats rows at keyset boundaries.
- **`compareTasksForQuery`** is the sort behind every `InMemoryDatabaseAdapter.getTasks` and `plugin-inmemorydb` result (`(created_at, id)` ascending, undefined-last).

No test file anywhere imports `validateTaskQueryPagination`, `validateQueryEntitiesPagination`, or `compareTasksForQuery` today; `compareMemoryIds` is only used as a harness helper in the browse-pagination route test, never asserted directly.

## What the tests pin

- **Validators (8 tests):** accept `undefined`/`0`, throw a boundary-prefixed `RangeError` (`queryEntities`/`getTasks`) on negative, fractional, `NaN`, `Infinity`, and non-integer values — and do not confuse the two boundaries.
- **`compareMemoryIds` (4 tests):** PostgreSQL-uuid order in both directions, mixed-case forms of the same id equal, ordering across the case boundary, reflexivity/antisymmetry.
- **`compareTasksForQuery` (4 tests):** earlier `createdAt` first, id tie-break, undefined `createdAt` last, case-normalized id tie-break.
